item.title: Economist discusses taxing the ultra wealthy and their impact on the economy
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with economist and wealth tax expert Gabriel Zucman about millionaire and billionaire taxes and their impact on the economy.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with economist and wealth tax expert Gabriel Zucman about millionaire and billionaire taxes and their impact on the economy.

item.title: Can Congress fix affordability? MIT's Daron Acemoglu weighs in
item.description: NPR's Scott Simon asks MIT economics professor Daron Acemoglu what, if anything, the coming Democratic majority in Congress can do about affordability. AI could be a big part of the equation.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Scott Simon asks MIT economics professor Daron Acemoglu what, if anything, the coming Democratic majority in Congress can do about affordability. AI could be a big part of the equation.

item.title: Hiring jumps: The economy added 165,000 jobs last month
item.description: The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.

(Image credit: Scott Olson)
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
item.description: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The U.S. economy added far more jobs in October than expected
item.description: Employers added 165,000 jobs last month, the Labor Department said on Friday, blowing past economists' expected gains of around 59,000 jobs.

item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody Analytics, for analysis of the post-midterm election economy.

item.title: With stubbornly high interest rates, some are reconsidering adjustable-rate mortgages
item.description: With the rates for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages at 7% or more, is it time to reconsider the far less popular adjustable-rate mortgage? New analysis shows that ARMs have paid off for borrowers.

item.title: AI shares sink after blue wave
item.description: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress -- and states across the country -- would crack down on AI data centers.

item.description: Democrats achieved stunning midterm victories. The party will take control of Congress next year. What does it mean for the economy?

item.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
item.description: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.
